data.why: The app generates its own fictitious example data at runtime: a 'Load example experiment' button on the Home screen populates every screen (zebrafish RT-qPCR dataset), and the qPCR screen offers downloadable example instrument files (QuantStudio xlsx, Rotor-Gene csv, generic csv) to test the import/auto-detect feature, so no files need to be copied or written.

goals: Plan a new RT-qPCR gene-expression experiment (species, tissue, groups, pools) and get a step schedule with calendar/WhatsApp reminders
Enter NanoDrop RNA quantification readings, check A260/280 and A260/230 quality criteria, and get cDNA synthesis volumes and a pipetting list
Import qPCR Ct data from an instrument export (QuantStudio or Rotor-Gene Q) or a generic table, with automatic blank and replicate checks
Compute relative gene expression (fold change / NRQ) using one or more reference genes with the qBase/ddCt model, including reference-gene stability (geNorm M, CV)
Run the appropriate statistical test (ANOVA/Dunnett, Welch, Kruskal-Wallis, t-test, etc.) with assumption checks and outlier detection, and produce publication-style bar charts and heatmaps
Generate a draft Methods and Results section (English/Portuguese) with the computed statistics filled in, and export figures/text as .docx or .zip

review.summary: The tree captures AmpliQA's purpose well, from experiment planning through NanoDrop QC, plate layout, reference-normalised fold change, assumption-driven statistics and figures to a bilingual methods draft, and the screens I opened all support their nodes. It needs fixes before filing: the core instrument-file import and saved-experiment resume are missing, a Kruskal-Wallis + Tukey app bug is recorded without comment, and the numbers further down rest on a target gene that was promoted to reference.
